We added wrapper but may not preserve __name__ etc? We used update_wrapper on _call with method, but we didn't set attributes of decorator wrappers? Wait original code: bound_method = partial(method.__get__(self,type(self))) then for dec in decorators: bound_method=dec(bound_method). That returns a function maybe partial again. Our change wraps only initial bound_method before applying decorators; but after applying decorators, the resulting bound_method may be a partial or other wrapper that lost attributes. The issue arises when decorator is applied to method_decorator(logger) where logger expects func.__name__ etc. In our case, logger uses @wraps(func). That inner function will have __name__ from original func? Actually wraps copies attributes from func. But if func is a partial, it lacks __name__. So we need to ensure that the object passed to decorator (the first argument) has __name__ attribute. The bound_method is a functools.partial; we can create a wrapper function _call that forwards and has same attributes as method. We used update_wrapper(_call, method). That sets __name__, etc. But then dec(bound_method) will receive this wrapper? Wait dec expects a function; our _call is a function with attributes of method. Good.

But we also need to preserve attributes after each decorator? The original code had _update_method_wrapper for each decorator and update_wrapper at end. That ensures wrappers get attributes from decorators. Our change may not affect that.
